title: Delhi to Gorakhpur Bus: Festive Season Travel Guide
summary: Timings, fares, boarding points and drop locations on the Delhi to Gorakhpur bus route, with booking advice for the Diwali and Chhath weeks.
body_markdown:
Three direct buses a day is the number that shapes every decision on this corridor. It is a long eastern run of roughly 750 km with a narrow departure window, and in the first half of November it carries families heading home for two festivals inside eight days. Scarcity, rather than fare, is what catches people out here.


# Planning the Delhi to Gorakhpur Bus for Festive Travel


The Delhi to Gorakhpur bus is an overnight service in the strictest sense, with every departure leaving in the early evening and arriving the following morning. That single fact determines how you plan the day before travel and the day you arrive.


## Why This Corridor Behaves Differently in November


Diwali falls on Sunday, 8 November 2026 and the main Chhath arghya on Sunday, 15 November, which sends two separate waves of travellers towards eastern Uttar Pradesh and onward into Bihar within the same fortnight.


This guide covers the practical shape of the journey: distance and duration, the departure window, fare range, boarding options in the capital, and where you actually get down. Wider connections appear on the[Gorakhpur bus booking page](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets/gorakhpur-bus-booking-online) for the city.


## Route Basics Worth Knowing Before You Book


These are the figures currently listed for the corridor, and they are the numbers to sanity check against your chosen departure.


**Detail** **Current listing**


Distance Approximately 751 km


Journey time About 9 hours 26 minutes in the route description, with a longer average shown in the summary panel


Daily departures 3 direct buses


Departure window Roughly 4:45 PM to 6:45 PM


Coach types Bharat Benz AC seater and sleeper, and AC semi sleeper and sleeper, all with onboard washroom


The listed duration differs between the summary panel and the route description, which is common on long corridors where actual running time swings with traffic. Treat both as indicative and check the time shown against the specific service on the[Delhi to Gorakhpur route page](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets/delhi-to-gorakhpur-bus-route) for your date.


## The Corridor Passes Through More Than You Expect


The run leaves Delhi through Noida and Jewar, crosses past Mathura and Agra, and then turns east through Lucknow, Barabanki, Faizabad and Ayodhya before Basti, Khalilabad and the final stretch into Gorakhpur.


That sequence matters for two reasons. It means the bus is on the road through the busiest section of the Lucknow corridor in the small hours, which is when festive traffic is lightest. It also means Ayodhya sits directly on the line, so pilgrims combining a temple visit with a family trip can plan around either the[Delhi to Ayodhya bus route](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets/delhi-to-ayodhya-bus-route) or a continued journey to Gorakhpur.


## Fares on This Route and What Changes Near the Festivals


Listed fares on the route currently run from about Rs 529 to Rs 868, with the summary panel showing a slightly wider band. The spread reflects coach type, seat position and how much of a given departure has already sold.


With only three buses a day, the cheaper inventory on peak evenings disappears quickly, and once it does there is no fourth departure to fall back on. The realistic advice for this corridor is not about chasing a lower fare but about securing a seat at all on the nights of 5 to 7 November and 12 to 13 November.


**Note:** Prices are approximately and may vary based on season, demand, and availability.


## Boarding in Delhi NCR Without Losing the Bus


Kashmere Gate ISBT is the anchor boarding point, with the counter inside the terminal near the metro exit. For anyone travelling from east Delhi or Ghaziabad, Anand Vihar ISBT has a counter inside the terminal building as well.


Beyond those two, the route lists a long spread of cab assisted pickups across Rohini, Pitampura, Shastri Nagar, Janakpuri, Dwarka Mor, Uttam Nagar, Ashram, Tughlakabad, Badarpur and Faridabad. These work well on ordinary evenings. On a festival eve, when your connecting cab is stuck in the same traffic as everyone else, a terminal boarding point is the safer choice, particularly as departures here are clustered inside a two hour window with nothing later to catch.


## Where the Bus Sets You Down in Gorakhpur


Nausad Chauraha on the Varanasi Road, near the HP pump opposite Badshah Lawn, is the primary drop point, with a partner office stop nearby. Both sit within a short auto or cab ride of the city, and local transport typically connects to hotels, Gorakhpur Junction and the airport within about 10 to 25 minutes depending on where you are headed.


Arriving in the morning is an advantage for anyone continuing to a smaller town. It leaves the full day for the onward leg, which is exactly what you need if the final destination is a village in Deoria, Kushinagar, Siwan or across the border into Bihar for Chhath.


## Meals and Conditions on a Long Overnight Run


Delhi to Gorakhpur is one of the three corridors, along with Delhi to Lucknow and Chennai to Coimbatore, where the Freemeal offer applies on Plus buses through the relevant coupon code at checkout. It is route specific rather than network wide, so check it at the payment step rather than assuming it.


Coaches on this route list charging points, blankets, water bottles, live tracking, a medical kit and an onboard washroom, with bio toilets on several services. Baggage is capped at 15 kg per passenger, which is easy to exceed when you are carrying sweets, gifts and clothing for a family stay of a week or more.


## Gorakhpur as a Base Rather Than a Destination


The city is worth a day in its own right. The Gorakhnath temple is the obvious stop, and the Ramgarh Tal lakefront has been developed enough to fill an evening comfortably.


For most festive travellers, though, Gorakhpur functions as a hub. Kushinagar sits roughly 52 km away and Ayodhya around 120 km, both manageable as day trips if your family leaves on a free day. Travellers coming from within the state can also use the[Lucknow to Gorakhpur bus route](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets/lucknow-to-gorakhpur-bus-route) as a shorter feeder leg rather than making the full run from Delhi.


## The Return Leg Is the Tighter Booking


Return services on the[Gorakhpur to Delhi bus route](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets/gorakhpur-to-delhi-bus-route) also run as a small number of evening departures, which makes the return the scarcer half of the trip. Demand concentrates on 10 and 11 November after Bhai Dooj, and again on 16 and 17 November once the Usha Arghya is complete.


Book both legs in one sitting. On a corridor with this few daily services, a return seat found at short notice is unlikely to exist at all, and the alternative usually means a train waitlist or a far longer road combination through Lucknow.


## Settling a Gorakhpur Trip for November


The corridor itself is straightforward: an early evening departure from Delhi, a night on the highway through Lucknow and Ayodhya, and a morning arrival at Nausad Chauraha with the day intact. What changes in November is that three buses are carrying the demand of a much larger week.


Fix the return date first, pick a terminal boarding point you can reach without depending on traffic, and get both legs booked through the second half of October. Everything else on the Delhi to Gorakhpur bus is an ordinary overnight journey.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### How long does the Delhi to Gorakhpur bus take?


The Delhi to Gorakhpur bus takes roughly 9 to 10 hours across about 751 km, though festive traffic can extend that noticeably on peak nights.


### What time do buses leave for Gorakhpur from Delhi?


Buses leave for Gorakhpur from Delhi within a narrow evening window of roughly 4:45 PM to 6:45 PM, making this an entirely overnight corridor.


### What is the Delhi to Gorakhpur bus fare?


The Delhi to Gorakhpur bus fare currently runs from about Rs 529 to Rs 868, depending on coach type, seat position and how early you book.


### How many buses run daily on this route?


Three direct buses run daily on this route, which is why seats on festive evenings need booking several weeks rather than several days ahead.


### Where do buses drop passengers in Gorakhpur?


Buses drop passengers at Nausad Chauraha on Varanasi Road near the HP pump, with a partner office stop close by for onward connections.


### Which boarding point in Delhi is most reliable?


Kashmere Gate ISBT is the most reliable boarding point because the counter sits inside the terminal, close to the metro exit and sheltered.


### Is a meal included on the Delhi to Gorakhpur bus?


Delhi to Gorakhpur is one of three routes where the Freemeal offer applies on Plus buses, applied through the relevant coupon code at checkout.


### Is a washroom available on board?


A washroom is available on board, with bio toilets fitted on several of the coaches currently operating between Delhi and Gorakhpur.


### When should I book for the Diwali and Chhath weeks?


Book through the second half of October for travel between 5 and 17 November, since only three daily departures serve this entire corridor.


### Does the bus pass through Ayodhya?


The route passes through Lucknow, Barabanki, Faizabad and Ayodhya before reaching Basti and Khalilabad on the final stretch to Gorakhpur.


### How far is Kushinagar from Gorakhpur?


Kushinagar is approximately 52 km from Gorakhpur, which makes it a comfortable day trip if your family leaves on a free day.


### How much luggage can I carry?


Luggage is capped at 15 kg per passenger, worth planning around when you are carrying festival sweets, gifts and clothing for a long stay.


### Are women only seats available on this corridor?


Women only seats can be selected at checkout on this corridor, and live GPS tracking is available through the app for the full journey.
